subtype: Approach: hopes that it will somehow work out without acting [Pitfall]
passage:
Thursday night. The rivers project is due tomorrow and I have not started. It's okay. I will do it later. Then it was dinner, then TV, then homework for the other subjects.
Now it's late and I have only drawn the map. Maybe Ma'am will say the date is extended, like she did once for the whole class. I am hoping really hard.
Mummy says she can't do it for me, but she is sitting next to me and cutting the paper. The map has a smudge. My eyes keep closing. It will be fine, I think. It will be fine.
Vasudha

qa.q: What has Vasudha finished so far?
qa.a: Vasudha has only drawn the map.

qa.q: What is Vasudha worried and hopeful about tonight?
qa.a: Vasudha is hoping that Ma'am will say the date is extended, and feels sleepy and a little worried.

qa.q: What would be a better plan for the next project?
qa.a: Vasudha could do a small part each day after school, since starting early means no rush and no need to hope for extra time.

qa.q: How might Mummy feel about sitting up with the project?
qa.a: Mummy may feel tired and concerned, since she is cutting paper late at night although she says she can't do it for Vasudha.

grounding: A child leaves a school project until the last night, keeps saying it will be fine, and hopes for an extension.
